title: God's Ultimate Clapback on Nineveh
paragraphs: § God Is Serious Business
A report on the whole Nineveh situation, just how God showed it to Nahum of Elkosh:

God does NOT play. Seriously, don't mess with Him. He gets back at His haters and stands up to anyone who comes against Him, full force. But, like, He's not just flying off the handle. He's got incredible power, but He's patient with it. Still, nobody gets away with anything. Sooner or later, you gotta pay up. You see tornadoes and hurricanes? That's just the dust kicking up where He walks. He can literally tell the ocean to dry up, and it does. All the rivers? Gone. The mountains of Bashan and Carmel? Withered. The forests of Lebanon? Wilted. Mountains quake in their roots, hills dissolve into mud. The whole planet is freaking out in front of Him. The whole world is in a full-blown panic. Who could even handle that kind of anger? Who can stand up to that fire? His rage is like a volcano erupting, and He smashes boulders like nothing.

But here's the flip side: God is good. He's your safe house when times get rough. He sees you when you're looking for help, and He's got you, no matter how bad things are. But for those who think they can just chill in their own little escape plans? Nah, He wipes them right off the map. You can't escape God. So why even try to scheme against Him? He's shutting all that down. If you're a troublemaker, you don't get a round two. You're like a pile of dry leaves someone just poured gasoline on. Poof. Up in flames.
§ A Think Tank for Lies
Nineveh is basically a headquarters for plotting against God. It's a think tank for lies that trick people and then stab them in the back.

And God's got a message about all this: “Even if you're on top of the world, getting all the applause and the votes, you'll get mowed down flat.” “Judah, I know I've put you through it, for real. But I'm done with that. From now on, I'm breaking that heavy thing off your neck and using it for firewood. I'm cutting you loose from whatever was holding you down.”

God's orders on Nineveh: “You're at the end of the line. It's all over with Nineveh. I'm tearing down your temple. Your gods and goddesses? Straight in the trash. I'm digging your grave myself. It's gonna be an unmarked one. You're a nobody—nah, you're less than a nobody!”

Look! Someone's running over the mountains—a messenger with the best news: peace! It's a holiday, Judah! Go celebrate! Worship God and get right with Him again! You don't have to worry about this enemy anymore. They're history. Close the books.

title: Nineveh's Epic Takedown
paragraphs: § Israel's Been to Hell and Back
The wrecking ball is coming! Post your guards, stock up on supplies. Get yourselves together, 'cause it's time for the main event.
God's restoring the honor of Jacob, the honor of Israel. Israel's been through it, for real. They've been to hell and back.

Their weapons are glinting in the sun, the soldiers looking fresh in their battle gear. The chariots are all polished and shiny, ready to roll out. It's like a whole forest of sharp spears, looking deadly on the horizon. The chariots are flooding the streets, taking over the public squares, glowing like torches in the sun, zipping around like lightning. The Assyrian king rallies his men, but they stagger and stumble. They rush to the walls to stop the invasion, but it's too late. Soldiers pour through the gates. The palace is getting wrecked. It's over pretty quick: Nineveh is getting stripped bare, totally doomed. The maids and slaves are crying, sounding like doves, beating their chests in sadness. Nineveh is like a bathtub with the plug pulled. People are yelling, "Do something! Do something!" but it's too late. Nineveh is empty in no time—nothing left. Then you hear other shouts: "Grab the silver! Grab the gold! It's a free-for-all! Take whatever you want!" It's all doom, damnation, and desolation. Hearts are sinking, knees are weak, people are throwing up, and everyone's face is pale. So, what happened to that big, bad Assyrian lion and all those so-called cute little cubs? What about the lion and lioness, all cozy with their cubs, acting so tough and fearless? What about the lion who always brought back fresh meat for his lioness and cubs, with the den piled high with bloody food for their royal feast?

"Assyria, I'm your enemy now," says God, the Commander of Heaven's Armies. "I'm gonna set your chariots on fire. They'll go up in smoke. 'Lion Country' will just be a field of dead bodies. Your whole war business is over—you're officially unemployed. No more wars for you to report, no more victories to brag about. You're out of the war game for good."

title: Nineveh's Epic Fail: It's Over
paragraphs: § Let the Nations Get Their Fill of the Ugly Truth

It's over for Murder City—a place full of lies, overflowing with stolen stuff, and totally addicted to violence! You hear the horns blasting, wheels rattling, horses going wild, and chariots swerving all over the place. Horsemen are charging, swords and spears out, and there are dead bodies rotting in the street, piled up like firewood. Bodies are literally in every gutter and alley, blocking every intersection! And the immoral women! So many immoral women. This city is fatally attractive, like a witch casting spells, luring whole nations into getting wrecked with its evil.

"I’m your enemy, Nineveh—yeah, me, God of the Angel Armies! I’m gonna rip off those seductive silk robes and put you on blast for the whole world to see. I’ll let every nation see the ugly truth of who you really are and always have been. I’m gonna throw filth at you and put you on a stage like an exhibit called ‘Unfaithful on Display.’ Everyone who sees you will be disgusted and say, ‘Nineveh is a total pigsty. What did we ever see in her? Who would even look twice? Ugh!’”
§ Past the Point of No Return

Do you really think you’re better than the Egyptian city of Thebes? It was sitting all proud and unbeatable on the Nile River, protected by the water like a wall. Ethiopia was its guard to the south, and Egypt was to the north. Put and Libya were strong allies, ready to jump in and help. But you know what happened to Thebes, right? The entire city was captured and marched off to a refugee camp. Their babies were smashed to death on the streets for everyone to see. Their best leaders were sold off at auction, and their famous people were put in chains. You can expect the exact same thing, Nineveh. You’ll be stumbling around like a bunch of drunk people, wondering what just hit you, looking for a place to pass out. All your defenses are like peach trees with ripe fruit, ready to be picked. One little shake and the peaches fall right into hungry mouths. Just face it: your soldiers are wimps. You’re a sitting duck. Your borders are wide open like doors, just inviting your enemies to come in. And who’s gonna stop them?

Go ahead, store up water for the siege. Strengthen your defenses. Get back to the basics: work the clay and make some bricks. But sorry, it's too late. Enemy fire is about to burn you up. Swords will chop you to pieces. You’ll be chewed up as if by locusts.

Yeah, like locusts—which is kinda ironic, because you guys are a plague of locusts yourselves. You’ve multiplied your shops and shopkeepers—more buyers and sellers than there are stars in the sky! A plague of locusts that just cleans out the whole neighborhood and then flies away. Your government officials are locusts, and your brokers and bankers are locusts too. At first, they’re all super helpful, full of smiles and promises. But later, when you come back with questions or problems, you’ll find out they’ve just flown off and are nowhere to be found.

King of Assyria! Your leaders, the ones in charge of taking care of your people, are busy doing everything else but their actual job. They’re failing, and your people are scattered and lost. There’s no one to look after them. You’re past the point of no return. Your wound is fatal. When the story of what happened to you gets out, the whole world will cheer and shout “Encore!” Your cruel evil has leaked into every corner of the world. Everyone has felt it and suffered because of you.
